resolution.note: Both refuters killed the one blocking finding (check_strategy_tie_in §4, line 21), and the scope refuter's first count is decisive: the finding silently tightened the rule's own bright line. The strategy doc's M5 section says the reveal is fragile and that nothing may name the three pieces *before the M4 evidence is read* — not before `diagnose-and-resend`'s header, which is where the finding relocated the boundary. By the time a student opens fork-the-worktree.md the M4 evidence has been read four times over: the Start here opener, `## Say what done-done means`, the whole of [Lecture: Reading the return], and `## Your mid-run worries hint at missing checks`. A finding that moves a documented constraint earlier than the doc states it is not enforcing the rule, it is writing a new one. Row stamps PASS:verify-refuted; the recorded REVISE stays as the record that the finding was filed and adjudicated, not overwritten.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Title (L1) 'Fork the worktree, carry the evidence' and 'The point' (L13) 'a worktree lets you run the same task twice as a split test' both lead with the constructive discipline. The line closest to violating this is the section header that used to read '## If the coordinates are missing' (pre-diff) — the diff renamed it to '## Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (L37), moving it off a failure-mode lead. The maintainer block's own 'Recovery ladder' note (L55) states the rationale directly: 'The section heading is neutral... because the first bullet is the normal path, not a fallback; a heading naming only the failure case contradicts its own opening line.' This is the rule being actively honoured, not skirted.

Harm this rule guards against: front-running a downstream teaching moment — here, M5's own explicitly load-bearing reveal ('The reveal is load-bearing and fragile: nothing may name the three pieces before the M4 evidence is read... a constraint on every beat in the module', doc §M5 in detail). The three pieces are reference artefact + plan.md + external verifier, reserved by design for diagnose-and-resend.md, whose own header (L15) reads 'What you build: a verifier, a reference, and a plan.md, each built against a failure you actually read' — clearly written as the FIRST reveal of these three names, tied to a felt failure. This file's L21 (new in this diff, confirmed via `git diff 61e7fc9..HEAD`) reads 'This module's work (diagnosis, verifier, reference, plan.md, and the re-send) runs in the worktree' — naming all three pieces as a flat inventory BEFORE the student opens diagnose-and-resend, stripped of any failure-specific connection. This is not a borderline read: two sibling files in the same module enforce the opposite discipline explicitly in their own maintainer blocks — reading-the-return.md L35 'Fixes-not-named discipline held: no reference / plan.md / verifier' and L49 'Don't pre-empt the three-pattern (reference / plan.md / verifier)... Naming the fixes here collapses the M5 contrast'; hooks-always-fire.md L19 goes further, deliberately keeping its own two verifier mentions generic ('a verifier', never 'the verifier you just wrote') for exactly this reason, at a placement between reading-the-return and this exercise. fork-the-worktree.md sits in the same slot (module TOC: reading-the-return → hooks-always-fire → fork-the-worktree → diagnose-and-resend) and is the one file in that sequence that breaks the discipline the other two visibly hold. The maintainer's L59 accept-note ('Phase 1 opens with the moved-in rationale, 2026-08-25, Antti-directed') authorises MOVING 'why the work runs in the worktree' content into this file from the module body — it says nothing about the specific three-pattern-naming risk, so it is not a dispositive accept-note against this finding (dispatch-preamble: an accept-note covers what it actually authorised, not everything adjacent to it).
